intent: Detection with a hair trigger: see the slot, enqueue the mission, pause - atomically.
change: The slot watch kind in the s2 engine: slot-yielding extractor contract, trigger policy committing observation, booking-task enqueue, and watch pause in one transaction, auto_book vs confirm-gated per-watch config, and re-arm semantics requiring a fresh extraction.
done_when: Unit tests prove trigger atomicity and re-arm-requires-fresh-check; integration tests on fakedmv fixtures prove a released slot fires exactly one enqueue with the watch paused, and check re-runs enqueue nothing while a task is pending.

proofs.claim: Before the engine knows a slot watch, the composed proof cannot load: the suite that runs a slot watch against fakedmv through the real ladder, store and trigger port fails at import because the watch package has no slot-trigger module.

With the slots value, the slot condition, the appeared-slot comparator and the transactional trigger in place, the same suite proves on fakedmv over a migrated Postgres that a released slot fires exactly one enqueue with the watch paused, that a re-run check enqueues nothing while the task is pending, that two concurrent checks arm once, that a pause whose observation cannot be written is rolled back, and that a re-arm alone triggers nothing until a fresh check extracts the slot again.

The unit rules hold: a slots value round-trips and identifies by its ids, the slot condition parses site, applicant and auto_book and refuses the rest, the comparator triggers on a slot that was not listed last time and never on the same listing twice, an empty calendar replays as an empty list rather than a broken selector, the door accepts a slot watch, and the check hands the trigger port the observation, the patch and the slot in one call.
The repository quality gate - lint, both typechecks, unit and integration tests under the coverage thresholds (100% on core), build and web build - passes with the slot watch kind in the tree.

intent: The booking arm: select, fill, submit, and never claim booked without the reference.
change: The registered fakedmv booking playbook: availability re-check, slot selection, applicant details from watch config, submit, confirmation-reference capture onto the task, optional UserIO confirm gate honoring auto_book, refused-slot-gone outcome when availability fails.
done_when: Integration tests via LocalProvider with scripted UserIO prove the booked path stores the fixture booking record and reference, the confirm gate asks and a decline cancels, auto_book skips the ask, and a missing slot at re-check yields refused-slot-gone without touching fixture state.

proofs.claim: Before the booking arm exists, its proof cannot load: the suite that drives a book_slot task through the fakedmv playbook on a pg-boss worker with a scripted person fails at import because the playbook module is not there.

With the playbook registered, the refused outcome in the lifecycle and the fixture minting a confirmation reference, the same suite proves via LocalProvider that the booked path leaves the fixture's booking record and stores its reference on the succeeded task, that the confirm gate asks and a decline cancels without touching the fixture, that auto_book skips the ask, that a slot missing at the re-check ends refused with the fixture untouched, and that a slot yanked between confirmation and submit ends refused too.

The unit rules hold: refused is a transition out of running into failed and nowhere else, the booking playbook reads the fixture's answers and the person's yes or no the way it claims, and the runner maps a refused step to a refused outcome.
The repository quality gate passes with the booking playbook, the refused cause and the fixture reference in the tree.

intent: Losing gracefully: the yanked slot re-arms the watch and tells the human, end to end.
change: The composed proof suite wiring trigger, playbook, re-arm, and s7 notifications: slot-yank race via the fixture control plane, refused-slot-gone re-arming the watch and notifying, booked-path notification, blocked-mode failure leaving the watch paused for attention.
done_when: Integration tests prove the full snipe (release → detect → confirm → booked → notified), the yank race (refused-slot-gone → re-armed → notified → a later release books), and blocked-mode pausing with notification - each with watch-state and fixture-state assertions.

proofs.claim: Before the reflex is closed, the composed proof cannot load: the suite that runs the watch engine, the task engine, the booking playbook and the re-arm consequences on one worker against fakedmv fails at import because the watch package has no snipe module.

With the consequence wrapper and the booking event on the notifier port, the same suite proves the full snipe (release, detect, confirm, booked, notified, watch left paused), the yank race (refused slot-gone, watch re-armed, notified, and a later release books), a decline re-arming the watch, and a hard-blocked site failing the mission with the watch left paused and the person told - each with watch-state and fixture-state assertions, and the task engine's settled hook is told the task the moment a run or an expiry settles it here (with a hook that throws left on the trail).
The unit rules hold: the notifier port names the booking event, and the consequence table maps each mission outcome and each answer to the watch state and the event it earns.
The repository quality gate passes with the snipe reflex, the booking event and the worker wiring in the tree.

intent: The person, not the process log, is who a watch tells: the notifier port reaches Telegram through the outbound door s3 built for it.
change: The spec production path says each watch event reaches the person through the s2 notifier port implemented over the bot sendToUser; in the tree the worker still runs createLogNotifier, so a trigger, a block, a degradation and every booking outcome this sprint added is one JSON line on stdout and nobody is told. Add packages/bot/src/notifier.ts: createTelegramNotifier(sendToUser, fallback) implements NotifierPort by rendering each of the four WatchEvent types as one plain sentence (the triggered reason with the watch url; blocked and degraded with their reason; a booking with the slot label, what became of the watch and the reference when booked) and sending it through sendToUser keyed by the event dedupKey; a NoBindingError hands the event to the fallback notifier so an unbound person loses nothing from the log, and a delivery that settled failed throws so the producer retries (the check tick, or the snipe sweep) instead of the port claiming delivery. Give the outbound door the key: deliveries gains a nullable unique dedup_key column with migration 0010, and createSendToUser accepts an optional third argument with dedupKey - a sent or pending delivery under that key is returned as it is, a failed one is retried on its own row, so at-least-once emission is delivered once. Export the notifier from packages/bot; in scripts/worker.mjs compose the telegram notifier over the same sendToUser the questions use, with the log notifier as its fallback, and keep the log notifier alone when TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is unset.
done_when: Unit proofs pin the four renderings, the unbound fallback and the failed-delivery throw; an integration proof over the real deliveries table shows one keyed event sent twice makes one delivery row and one message, a failed keyed delivery is retried on the same row by the next emission, and unkeyed sends are unchanged; the existing outbound, user-io and reminder proofs stay green; the repository gate passes with the migration in the tree.

proofs.claim: Before the adapter exists, the unit suite that renders each watch event as the sentence the person receives, hands an unbound person to the fallback and throws on a failed delivery cannot load: the bot package has no notifier module.

The adapter renders a trigger, a block, a degradation and each booking outcome as one plain sentence, sends it through the outbound door keyed by the event's dedup key, hands the event to the fallback notifier when the person has no chat bound, and throws when the delivery settled failed so the producer retries.

Over the real deliveries table, one keyed event emitted twice makes one delivery row and one message, a failed keyed delivery is retried on its own row by the next emission, an unkeyed send is unchanged, and the notifier proves the whole door end to end: a recorded chat sender receives the sentence once.
The repository quality gate passes with the Telegram notifier, the keyed outbound door and its migration in the tree.

intent: The booking arm reads the calendar by what the fixture promises to keep, not by the classes it promises to rotate.
change: packages/playbooks/src/fakedmv/booking.ts finds the calendar by ul.dmv-slots and the slot entry by li.dmv-slot, the normal-layout classes fakedmv rotates in redesign mode (added to fakedmv this sprint, hostile-mode-surfaces spec); under redesign the availability step reports that fakedmv did not show its calendar while the calendar is on the page, the mission fails, and the snipe pauses the watch for attention with a false reason. The sibling fakegym playbook locates by data-testid throughout. Locate by the surface redesign keeps byte-identical: the calendar by its Appointments heading or the no-slots and slot-* data-testid hooks, the entry by a [data-testid^=slot-] element containing the slot label as exact text, the button by its accessible name; keep the slot-gone and booked readings unchanged.
done_when: The fakedmv integration proof books the slot under redesign mode with the fixture booking record and the reference on the task, reads a yanked slot as slot-gone under redesign, and every existing fakedmv booking case stays green; the booking unit suite and the repository gate pass.

proofs.claim: Before the locators change, the fakedmv integration proof's redesign case fails: the availability step reports that fakedmv did not show its calendar while the redesigned calendar lists the slot.

expected.failure_signature: fakedmv did not show its calendar

proofs.claim: The booking playbook books the slot under redesign mode with the fixture's booking record and the reference on the task, reads a yanked slot as slot-gone under redesign, and every existing fakedmv booking case still holds.
The booking unit rules - the gate question and its yes, the answer parser and the outcome table - are unchanged by the locator change.
The repository quality gate passes with the booking playbook reading the fixture's stable surface.
